#XRP and how we stand right now. 
Current Developments in Japan Regarding XRP (as of December 18, 2025)Japan remains a key hub for XRP adoption, primarily through its long-standing partnership between Ripple and SBI Holdings. While no major nationwide mandate has been announced today, the focus is on an impending Bank of Japan (BOJ) interest rate decision tomorrow (December 19), which is creating market turbulence for XRP and broader crypto. Here's a breakdown of what's happening right now:1. BOJ Rate Hike Expectations and Market Impact

The BOJ is widely expected to raise rates to 0.75% at 10:00 PM ET tonight (tomorrow morning in Japan), with odds at 98%.@DefiWimarThis follows hikes in July 2024 and January 2025, and it's sparking fears of a yen carry trade unwind—where trillions in borrowed yen could flow back to Japan, pressuring global https://t.co/TIGt5ccGGb

XRP has slumped below $2 (currently around $1.85–$1.90), down 6% recently, amid these yen carry trade concerns and surging 10-year Japanese Government Bond (JGB) yields at 1.98%.fxempire.com +1Analysts warn this could lead to further downside for XRP, Bitcoin, and Ethereum, with potential 10–30% drops in crypto markets https://t.co/hZfoElZr3K

Community speculation on X ties this to XRP's potential role: A carry trade collapse could force Japanese banks (holding ~$7–10 trillion in assets) to adopt XRP for efficient cross-border settlements to cut https://t.co/DTyqwSNtXQ +1SBI CEO Yoshitaka Kitao has long claimed "every bank in Japan will use XRP by 2025," and with the year ending, tomorrow's hike is seen as a possible catalyst.

2. Recent Partnership Announcements

This aims to make XRP a yield-bearing asset, enhancing its utility for institutional investors in Japan.Yesterday (December 17), SBI Ripple Asia partnered with Doppler Finance to explore XRP-based yield products and real-world asset (RWA) tokenization on the XRP Ledger (XRPL).coindesk.com +1

Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin is set for launch in Japan by Q1 2026, complementing XRP in liquidity and https://t.co/xLaMJ3bfgv

3. Broader Adoption and Regulatory Moves

Japan is accelerating plans to classify XRP as a financial product by Q2 2026, enabling broader integration into banking systems.@CoinvoAll banks are expected to go live on XRPL by Q1 2026, per SBI statements.

Ripple is developing a zero-knowledge identity verification system on XRPL, positioning it as infrastructure for Japan's tokenized economy, including identity, compliance, and asset management.

Ongoing real-world use: SBI Remit uses XRP via Ripple's On-Demand Liquidity (ODL) for remittances to Southeast Asia (e.g., Philippines, Vietnam), handling significant volume.@xspectDS~80 banks are already connected via RippleNet.@xspectDS

Analyst Michael Gayed highlights Japan as a test case for scaled XRP adoption due to its remittance needs, FX efficiency demands, and crypto-friendly regs since 2017.If widely adopted, price models suggest $16+ per XRP in optimistic scenarios.

data.raw_text:
2025 has been an exhilarating year for me, not because my portfolio has substantially appreciated, but many of my predictions that have been ridiculed by others turn out to be spot on

1. US geopolitical pivot
China has set a trap for US to either go for an arms race or back off. Trump decided US cannot afford a such a race and chose to back off, confirmed by 2025 National Security Strategy where it admits US can no longer contain China alone and has to rely on regional allies to help. Japan is eager to do so, South Korea already decline, Philippines is willing but not capable, Australia is way too far.
What a mess!

2. Trump tariff backfires spectacularly 
Even before Liberation Day, I said tariff will backfire. Trump’s scorched earth strategy of hitting friends and foes created frictions among allies, and forceful retaliation from China. Eventually, Trump had to back off after 5 rounds of negotiations with China

3. Reshoring manufacturing is a pipe dream 
I pointed out US does not have electricity, grid, infrastructure, skilled workers to reshore manufacturing. MAGA crowd ridiculed me and said US has plenty of oil reserves and skilled workers that have been made unemployed due to illegal migrants. Now AI bubble is being questioned and people find out data centers building will have to slow down because US does not have power grid to support this growth

4. US cannot contain China in AI development 
Deepseek was a shock for US AI  circle, but there are many unknown Chinese companies developing new products and technologies along the AI value chain. Local produced DUV machines already in mass production, EUV is being tested. Many find this development shocking. I have always stated
Innovation = # of engineers X # of hours they work
China has advantages on both elements

5. Russia will force Ukraine to capitulate 
When paid propagandists were saying Russia was using washing machine chips to make missiles and Russian army was collapsing, I said Ukraine will have to capitulate as NATO support cannot be sustainable. After collapsing EU economy and Trump unwilling to foot the bill anymore, we are finally in the “peace” discussion

6. #Gold #Silver will rally due to price setting in Asia
SGE gold premium has pulled spot price up over time and silver rally after years of supply deficit were all due to Asia willingness to pay more for physical metals. With draining inventory in LBMA/COMEX, global spot price had to move up and they do in shocking fashion in 2025

7. Evolution into 2 global trade systems using different trade settlement mechanisms 
The world will have 2 parallel trade systems of China+ and US+. Trump tariff expedites this development. Despite decrease of China US trade in 2025, China experiences the highest trade and surplus with its partners. China and its partners are also settling their trade increasingly using local currencies instead of USD

I definitely do not consider myself smart and there are many others smarter than me. But I learned early in my career to put away any prejudice and subjectivity when analyzing any situation. Some common prejudices like religion, political ideology, nationality/ethnicity, perception of right vs wrong will easily lead you down the wrong path

When doing analyses, always question the source of information and your initial assessment. Ask yourself “Does it make sense”. Only through vigorous analysis and assessment will you be able to come up with more accurate view of the problem.
